subject: NimbusPay hosted API: monthly volume & peak TPS — next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@nimbuspay.com>, Carlos Rivera <c.rivera@nimbuspay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 May 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: NimbusPay hosted API: post-call recap & next steps

Hi Emma / Carlos — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap so we have a shared starting point and clear next steps.

What we discussed (high level)
- Primary use: real-time payment-chat assistance + fraud signal enrichment.
- Expected baseline monthly usage: rough estimate range (you said you'd confirm): 200–300M tokens/mo to start, plan to scale.
- Growth target: additional seasonal peaks and feature launches could push to ~1B+ tokens/mo within 6–9 months.
- Peak TPS requirement: sustained ~30–40 TPS during business hours, with short bursts up to ~80 TPS for ~20–60s during promotions.
- Budget posture: procurement prefers an upper-bound target of $/1M tokens that keeps run-rate <$50k/mo initially — you mentioned procurement has a target around $900–1,200 per 1M tokens, but will confirm.

What I need from you to finalize a proposal
1) Please fill the attached volume template with your current monthly baseline, expected month-over-month growth, and an expected worst-case spike duration — I attached "nimbus_volume_template.xlsx".
2) Confirm whether the 80 TPS spikes are single-region or global (helps sizing).
3) Any hard constraints on budget or PO timeline (e.g., must sign by end of month).

What we'll do next
- Marissa will draft three pricing options: pay-as-you-go, committed slab, and a reserved/SLA-backed option with burst allowances.
- I'll produce a preliminary unit-econ estimate ($/1M tokens) and a recommended deployment pattern (caching/batching suggestions to reduce spend).
- If numbers look good, we can get a short follow-up with procurement and share a DocuSign for a 6–12 month commit.

Attachments: nimbus_volume_template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Proposed follow-up: 30-min call Friday 10:30am PT to review the filled template and our preliminary numbers — does that work?

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

——

Subject: Re: NimbusPay hosted API: post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Rafael — good summary. Attaching the filled template (see attachment) and answering a few questions inline.

Baseline & growth (from attached):
- Current baseline (May): 250M tokens/mo (chat + enrichment).
- Expected growth: conservative plan to reach 600M by end of Q3, optimistic ramp to ~1.2B by Dec if new merchant integrations go live.

Peak behavior:
- Sustained TPS: 35 TPS during peak windows.
- Short spikes: up to 80 TPS for ~30s during marketing pushes; these are single-region for now (US-east), likely to be multi-region later in the year.

Budget target and procurement
- Procurement has sign-off flexibility but they asked the sales team to target a long-term blended cost of ~$950 per 1M tokens as an internal goal — not a hard limit but helps prioritization.
- Timeline: procurement review meeting next Wed (May 16). If we have a proposal and ballpark pricing by Monday (May 14) they can put a PO on the agenda.

Questions:
- How does Redwood treat short-duration spikes for billing? Do you have burst credits or an amortized approach?
- Can caching reduce token count for our enrichment calls (those lookups are often identical across sessions)?

Attachment: nimbus_volume_template_filled.xlsx (sent as "nimbus_volume_template.xlsx")

Cheers,
Emma Liu

emma.liu@nimbuspay.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NimbusPay hosted API: post-call recap & next steps

Emma — perfect, thanks for the filled numbers; very helpful. A few quick items from our side after reviewing the template:

1) Billing for spikes: we support two common approaches:
   - Pay-as-you-go: you pay per-token for everything; spikes are billed at the same unit rate.
   - Committed slab + burst: you buy a committed token slab (monthly) at a discounted rate and get a burst allowance (or pre-negotiated overage rate) for short spikes. For short spikes of 30s–1min we typically size burst headroom and amortize costs in the commitment model to avoid huge overage surprises.

2) Caching opportunity: yes — for enrichment/lookup calls we often see 20–40% token reduction with prefix caching + condensed prompts. If you can isolate enrichment calls in the template rows I’ll run a quick estimate and include conservative savings in the unit-econ.

Preliminary unit economics (very rough) based on current volumes:
- Baseline (250M/mo) @ pay-as-you-go estimate: ~$1,600 / 1M tokens (gross list) -> ~ $400k/mo (gross).
- Committed 6–12mo slab (example): discount to ~$950 / 1M tokens -> ~ $237.5k/mo at 250M baseline.
- Reserved SLA-backed (dedicated capacity) for consistent 35 TPS sustained: effective $700 / 1M tokens (includes burst headroom).

I attached a quick TPS profile snapshot (nimbus_qps_profile.png) showing the sustained vs spike windows you provided.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa to produce a formal price comparison (PAYG vs committed vs reserved) with exact numbers for 3 scenarios (250M baseline, 600M mid, 1.2B high).
- I’ll draft a short SOW and draft PO language you can share with procurement.
- If helpful, we can open a short trial (30 days) with a committed credit and test caching to capture token savings.

Can you confirm the procurement meeting on May 16 is the decision point? If so, we’ll aim to have a formal proposal in your hands by EOD Monday (May 14).

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai

[Attachment: nimbus_qps_profile.png (image)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing options & recommended slab for NimbusPay

Emma — looping in a concise pricing table and recommendation based on Rafael’s unit-econ and your volume profile.

Pricing bands (illustrative, final numbers will be in the proposal):
- Pay-as-you-go (no commit): $1,600 / 1M tokens. Good for flexibility, higher marginal cost.
- Committed slab (6–12 month): $950 / 1M tokens at 250M committed. Tiered discounts above 500M and 1B. Committed slab includes a measured burst allowance to cover short spikes.
- Reserved/SLA (dedicated capacity): $700 / 1M tokens with 99.95% latency SLA and pre-provisioned burst headroom (best for latency-sensitive production).

Recommendation: Given the growth curve you shared, the committed slab (6–12mo) is the most pragmatic starting point: it lowers unit cost near your procurement target (~$950 / 1M) while preserving capacity to grow into higher discounts. We can include a 30-day pilot credit so engineering can validate caching gains before commit.

Next steps we’ll action this morning:
1) Drafted proposal + pricing worksheet for three scenarios (attached to the HubSpot deal).
2) Draft DocuSign with standard 6-month committed slab + optional rollover to 12 months. Link: https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/NP-2028-034
3) Rafael & Vivek available to join procurement meeting on May 16 if you want technical + commercial coverage.

If this looks right, we’ll send the formal proposal by EOD Monday (May 14).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
